brief: A recap of Goldman derivatives strategist Brian Garrett's Weekend Prep note, with Nomura's Charlie McElligott quoted on the same volatility collapse. The chain: the jobs number reinforced Warsh's read that the labor market is solid, so the Fed decision now turns on inflation, hike odds for next week's meeting are 60% against a Goldman house view of no hike, and yet the S&P surface prices Friday's CPI session at a 100bps straddle, which Garrett treats as three days of free gamma. Implied vol across index and singles is at year-to-date lows, tech vol has repriced from eye wateringly expensive to extremely reasonable, and six-month S&P realized correlation is an almost unprecedented 11, matched only by Feb 2007 and Jan 2018, which Garrett says is unsustainable and has historically ended in a starburst of index vol convexity. Goldman prime brokerage net and gross are back at post-liberation day lows, and S&P rallies are almost twice as volatile as sell offs, which Garrett reads as a market not full on exposure. Separately the desk calls the long end the greater risk, with the 30yr yield 1-month average north of 5.2% for the first time since 2003.
